summary: Monroe County lookout built in 1915 by a patrolman and taken over by the Pocono Protective Fire Association; no later source found.

events.note: Report for 1915 says Patrolman Primrose built the look-out at Resica.
Lookout became property of the Pocono Protective Fire Association after an employee erected it under a co-operative agreement.

evidence.supports: Page heading gives the county as Monroe
1915: Patrolman Primrose built a look-out at Resica
evidence.quote: Patrolman Primrose built a look-out at Resica which serves the purpose of viewing the outlying regions.

evidence.supports: Lookout became property of the Pocono Protective Fire Association, erected by an employee under the co-operative agreement
evidence.quote: This Look-out also became the property of the Pocono Protective Fire Association because of its erection by an employee under the co-operative agreement.

evidence.supports: Page note: the 1915 remark refers to this tower and the one on Mt. Pocono

evidence.supports: Both lookouts (this one and the one on Mt. Pocono) are rustic wooden structures
evidence.quote: Both look-outs are rustic wooden structures.

evidence.supports: Remark is from the Report of the Chief Forest Fire Warden for 1915
evidence.quote: Report of the Chief Forest Fire Warden for 1915

evidence.supports: Pocono Protective Fire Association organized in 1902 to build wooden fire towers to watch over members' lands
evidence.quote: In 1902, the Pocono Protective Fire Association, the first of its kind in the United States, organized and collected funds from its members to construct wooden fire towers to monitor their lands.

notes_for_editor: One page with a single 1915 report extract; no register entry in the FFLOS or NHLR caches; no status, access or later history found in two searches. The design key comes from the sentence that describes both this lookout and one on Mt. Pocono, so it is shared with that other tower. The heading Pine Mountain and the record's nearest-town field are not a verified location; the record's coordinates were not checked. Do not merge with the Franklin County Pine Mountain tower (firetower.org) or the other Pine Mountain page on easternuslookouts, which are different sites.
